held.why: REFUSED: Quotations and lines are right ('passed the noticeboard' l.37, 'September football trials' l.38, 'It won't fit me next year.' l.47), and 'September trials belong to next year too' is a fair school-year inference (Ilya's 'When we're in Year Six', l.15). But the step the key rests on, 'he is already giving up on next year', is asserted, not shown: the only evidence cited is a size reason ('won't fit me'), which a child will read as simply outgrowing the jumper. Ground it in lines that show the reason is not the whole story, e.g. he returns even a leaver's cardigan (l.14) yet puts his own named jumper in 'the Friday box' (l.33), and Miss Bhatt 'looked at him for a second or two longer than the answer needed' (l.48). The key remains the one defensible answer; the fault is in the script.
